intervention: Keep identical predictive files, instrument states, old acquisition plan and textual lessons; remove only the newly consolidated program and its manifest entry.
learning: Begin with the earlier LLM-authored acquisition-only program. Execute it on a training apparatus, return actual paid outcomes, revise it, and execute the revised procedure. Practice allows 768 observation rows to accommodate repeated method revision; transfer keeps the same 240-row allowance in both conditions. No host-written sampling or fitting policy is supplied.
publication: A revised current method must actually export the submitted predictor through its own post-acquisition steps; that predictor must pass ordinary fresh confirmation. This tests a practiced method, not an independently validated transferable procedure.
transfer: Only the practiced method and common verbal lesson carry over. Restore the original pre-practice predictive snapshot in both conditions; do not transfer practice-fitted instruments or predictors. Four independent transfer tasks follow method freezing.
terminal_order: Generate terminal labels only after all four transfer agents stop learning.
cost_scope: Include original learning, seed-method consolidation and paid practice as common learning costs once per condition, separately from transfer.
limitations: One training apparatus and one paired transfer apparatus in fixed operator families. The model is explicitly tasked with method practice; meaningful program revision and independent transfer benefit require the actual execution traces and comparisons.
support_diagnostics: Response fitting also reports the consumed instrument's residuals on current already-paid meter readings, with scoring charged. These are consistency diagnostics, possibly including fitting evidence, not fresh confirmation. They do not mutate the instrument, remove candidates, acquire evidence or choose a repair; all knowledge conditions receive them.
